answer: Fingerprints, not faces, should earn standing: record each identity's phrasing, timing and characteristic errors, then cluster those fingerprints continuously. A farmer running one script behind many masks leaves the same trail from jetty to haven, so near-identical clusters merge and are paid once, however many names they wear. Like water vanishing into karst, cloned work cannot hide its shared source — distinct behaviour stays distinct, and faking difference costs as much as being real.
